title: THE SINGAPORE OPENER · HYBRID STRENGTH
vibe: RE-ENTRY · Eleven days since the last logged session, twelve time zones crossed, and a hotel gym you have never trained in. This is not the day to prove anything. It is the day to start the block clean. One kettlebell, a pair of dumbbells, a treadmill that reads in kilometres, and forty-five minutes. The new thing today is not a movement, it is the SHAPE: the run is woven through the lifting instead of parked at the end, which is the first time this program has ever built a session that way.
why: Three things are different about today and all three are deliberate. First, the source. Every seeded session in this log has come from the same two books — Neupert's 102 and the single-bell muscle-building manual — and nine of the twelve seeded days came from Neupert alone. That is why the sessions started converging: the shapes rotate, but they rotate inside one tradition. Today's structure comes from somewhere genuinely new: Ladder's Project Alpha, Coach Sam Tooley's hybrid strength split, whose equipment list is literally dumbbells and a treadmill and whose signature is fusing the lift and the run into one continuous piece rather than running them as separate blocks. Second, the arc. Look at the last month — mobility warm-up, kettlebell block, treadmill, core finisher, cooldown, in that order, almost every time. The format labels changed; the skeleton never did. Today the treadmill is not a block, it is the connective tissue of Block 2, and you will step on and off it six times. Third, the units. Your entire profile is written in mph because the Bowflex console reads in mph. This machine reads in km/h, so every number below is converted, and the ~5% low calibration you learned on your own treadmill does not transfer to a machine you have never run on. Trust the belt's distance readout and your own legs, not a remembered offset. On the loading: single 20 kg bell because you asked to keep it simple, and 20 kg is 44 lb — you press a pair of 40s at home, so a single bell overhead is well inside your range, not a concession. The run in Block 2 totals fifteen minutes at your easy pace, which is roughly your habitual two miles. That is on purpose. Your daily run is a fixed input, not a slot to fill, so today it lives inside the session instead of getting stacked on top of it.

blocks.title: WARM-UP · MOVEMENT PREP, NOT A RITUAL
blocks.meta: ~6 min · treadmill + floor · continuous, no stopping · borrowed wholesale from how Ladder opens a session
blocks.text: This is a departure from the mobility ritual that has opened every session in this log, and it is worth naming why. Ladder does not run a standalone mobility segment — they fold dynamic prep straight into the front of the workout, each piece on its own short clock, and it flows directly into the first working set. That is what this is. Nothing here is held, nothing is counted in sets. Start on the belt: three minutes, walk at 5.5 km/h and climb to an easy jog around 9 km/h by the end, incline 2%. Step off and go straight into the floor work with no break. Good Morning, hands behind your head, hinge and stand, 30 seconds. Knee Hug to Lunge, walking, pull the knee to your chest then step straight into a long lunge, 40 seconds. Chest Opener, big arm sweeps with a slight rotation each way, 30 seconds — do these properly, you have been on a plane. Skip in place building speed, 30 seconds. Then pick up the bell. If anything feels genuinely locked up from the flight, spend an extra minute on the chest opener and the lunge, and take it out of nowhere else.

blocks.title: BLOCK 1 · SINGLE-BELL STRENGTH
blocks.meta: ~14 min · one 20 kg kettlebell · 4 rounds · straight sets, real rest · alternate A1 and A2, rest 60-75s after each pair
blocks.format: STRAIGHT-SET STRENGTH · no clock on the work, only on the rest · rotated off the density and circuit formats that dominated late July and early August
blocks.workRest: Four rounds. Front squat, rest about thirty seconds, press, rest sixty to seventy-five seconds, repeat. This is the block where you are allowed to be patient — nothing here is for time and there is no round target to chase. You are eleven days off and the point of this block is to remind your body what a loaded squat and a loaded press feel like, at a weight that is honest but not a test. If round four feels strong, that is information for the rest of the week, not a reason to add a fifth.

items.name: A1 · KB FRONT SQUAT · 8 reps
items.detail: 20 kg in the rack position, one bell, elbow tucked inside the knee at the bottom. Alternate which side the bell sits on each round — right, left, right, left — so both sides get two rounds of asymmetric loading. That off-centre load is doing quiet anti-lateral-flexion work on every single rep, which is why this block does not need a separate core piece bolted onto it. Sit down between your heels, knees tracking out, chest tall. Eight clean reps, and the last one should look like the first.

items.name: A2 · KB STRICT PRESS · 6 reps per side
items.detail: 20 kg, strict, no leg drive, no push press. Six on the right, six on the left, that is one round. Twenty kilos is forty-four pounds and you press a matched pair of 40 lb bells at home, so a single bell overhead is well within you — but you have been off for eleven days and you just spent a long time in a seat, so if the first round grinds or the lockout wanders, take the 16 kg and finish all four rounds there. Dropping the load to keep the reps clean is the correct call; grinding a sloppy press on day one of a ten-day block is not. Ribs down, glutes tight, punch straight up past your ear.

items.name: THE CHOICE TO MAKE
items.detail: The gym has 12, 16 and 20. Today is written at 20 for both movements. Report back which one you actually pressed, because that single data point sets the loading for the whole Singapore block — if 20 is a comfortable strict six per side, the rest of the trip gets programmed heavier than anything in your log, and if it is not, we know that too.

blocks.text: Straight sets with full rest is the format your log has seen least in the last three weeks. Late July and early August were dominated by density work — gauntlets, EMOMs, circuits, a Total Body Smoker, a chipper. The last true heavy-slow day was the 2nd. Coming off eleven days of nothing, the right re-entry is unhurried strength at a moderate load, not a metabolic session that punishes you for being detrained. The metabolic work is in Block 2 where it belongs.

blocks.title: BLOCK 2 · HYBRID INTERVALS
blocks.meta: ~18 min · treadmill + dumbbells · 3 rounds · step off the belt straight into the weights · transitions are the only rest
blocks.format: HYBRID STRENGTH · run and lift interleaved in one continuous piece · the Project Alpha signature and a shape this program has never run
blocks.workRest: Three rounds, and a round is: four minutes running, then straight off the belt to the dumbbells, then straight back on. There is no programmed rest — the walk from the treadmill to the rack and back is the rest. Set the belt speed once and leave it; you should be stepping on at the same speed in round three as in round one. This is the piece that makes today different from every other session in this log. Your run has always been a block with a start and an end, usually near the end of the session. Here it is the spine of the workout and the lifting hangs off it. Expect the third run to feel harder than the first at identical speed, and expect that to be the interesting part.

items.name: RUN · 4:00 @ 12.2 to 12.9 km/h
items.detail: That converts to roughly 4:55 to 4:40 per kilometre, or 7:55 to 7:30 per mile — your own easy aerobic band, straight off your watch history, not a slowed-down version of it. Nothing here asks you to hold back and nothing here is a tempo either. Pick a number in that band on the first round and hold the same number all three times. Zero incline. Cadence quick, around 168 to 172, short steps. IMPORTANT: this is not your Bowflex. You learned that your home console reads about 5% low; you have no idea what this machine does, so do not carry that correction over. Watch the distance readout — three rounds should put roughly 3.1 to 3.3 km on the belt, plus the warm-up jog.

items.name: DB ROMANIAN DEADLIFT · 12 reps
items.detail: Both dumbbells, hinge at the hip, soft knees, weights tracking down the front of your thighs, chest over the bar path. Stop when your hamstrings tell you the range is done, not when the weights hit the floor. Pick a load that leaves two solid reps in the tank on the third round — you will not know what that is on round one, so err lighter and let round two tell you. This is the hinge for the day and it is the pattern most likely to be stiff after a flight, so the first set is a feeling-out set on purpose.

items.name: DB SINGLE-ARM ROW · 10 reps per side
items.detail: One hand braced on a bench or a rack upright, one dumbbell, ten a side. Pull to the hip, not to the armpit. This is the only true pull in the session and it is deliberately unilateral — Ladder programs every single-side movement as its own separate timed line item rather than a footnote, and that structural habit is worth copying, because it is exactly where your log has been thinnest. Then straight back onto the belt.

items.name: IF ROUND 2 IS A WALL
items.detail: Stop at two rounds and go to Block 3. Eleven days off plus twelve time zones is a real thing and calling it at two rounds is a legitimate first session, not a failure. What is NOT the right adjustment is slowing the run down to survive a third round — the run speed is the one number in this session that stays fixed. Cut rounds, never cut pace.

blocks.text: This shape came out of studying how Ladder builds. Their Project Alpha program, Coach Sam Tooley, is described as hybrid strength training — blending strength and endurance work, dumbbells and a treadmill, three of its six days built exactly like this. It is the closest thing in their catalogue to what you already are, a runner who lifts, and the equipment list matches this hotel gym precisely. Every run in your log to date has been a discrete block. This is the first time the running and the lifting are the same piece of work.

blocks.title: BLOCK 3 · CARRY & MIDLINE
blocks.meta: ~7 min · 20 kg bell + bodyweight · the dedicated core block · short on purpose
blocks.format: LOADED CARRY + STATIC MIDLINE · rotated off the crawl-and-carry gauntlet that closed the last session
blocks.workRest: Straight through, minimal rest, roughly seven minutes total. This is the end of the session and it is intentionally the shortest block on the page. You have already done anti-lateral-flexion work all through Block 1 with the offset front squat rack; this just finishes the job and gets you off the floor.

items.name: SUITCASE CARRY · 40 m per side, 2 rounds
items.detail: 20 kg in one hand, walk forty metres or whatever the longest clear stretch of that gym is, then switch hands and walk back. Two full down-and-backs. Level shoulders, no lean toward the weight, no hitch in the hip — walk like your hand is empty. Every step is a rep of not bending sideways, and this is the piece that most directly protects the low back that keeps showing up stiff in your check-ins.

items.name: SIDE PLANK · 0:30 per side, 2 rounds
items.detail: On the elbow, hips stacked and driven up, body in one line from ear to ankle. Thirty seconds a side, twice. If thirty is easy, do not add time — lift the top leg instead.

items.name: HOLLOW HOLD · 0:30, 2 rounds
items.detail: Flat on your back, low back pressed into the floor, shoulder blades and legs both off the ground. Thirty seconds, twice. The moment your low back peels off the floor the set is over — bend the knees or bring the arms to your sides and keep holding rather than losing the position.

blocks.text: Standing rule: every session ends with a dedicated midline block. It stays. But it is seven minutes today rather than ten, because Block 1's offset kettlebell rack and Block 2's unilateral rows already loaded the midline asymmetrically for half an hour, and because this is a re-entry session that should leave you wanting tomorrow rather than wrecked.

blocks.title: COOLDOWN
blocks.meta: ~4 min · hips and hamstrings from the RDLs, shoulders from the presses, calves from the run · plus a flight to undo
blocks.text: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch, 45s per side — you sat for a very long time to get here and this is the one that pays. Standing or seated hamstring stretch, 45s per side, after twelve RDLs. Doorway or wall chest stretch, 45s per side, to open the front of the shoulder after the presses. Calf stretch against a wall, 30s per side, straight knee then bent knee. Finish with two minutes flat on your back, legs up against the wall, breathing slow through your nose — that one is as much for the jet lag as the training. Report back: which bell you pressed in Block 1, how many rounds of Block 2 you finished and at what belt speed, total distance the treadmill showed, and how the body actually felt, because that sets the loading for the next nine days.

timer.emomUnit: No EMOM and no AMRAP today. Block 1 is untimed straight sets — use the timer only for the 60-75s rest between pairs. Block 2 runs off a 4:00 countdown for each run segment, three times, with no clock at all on the dumbbell work. Block 3 is by distance and a 30-second hold timer. The treadmill's own distance readout is the number that matters most today.
